headline: All animals share a common ancestor—evolution branched from one origin into millions of species
universal_truth: Diversity arises from unity; differences emerge from common origins over time
fun_facts: You share about 60% of your DNA with a banana—and 85% with a mouse
All life on Earth shares the same genetic code—suggesting a single origin
The last common ancestor of all animals lived about 650 million years ago
discussion_questions: How does knowing you're related to all animals change how you see them?
What evidence shows that different species are related?
Why do related animals sometimes look so different?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You and a butterfly share an ancestor. So do you and a fish, a worm, a sponge. Every animal on Earth—from elephants to insects—traces back to a common origin. We're all distant cousins on one enormous family tree.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Animals look incredibly different—how can a whale be related to a fly? What evidence convinced scientists that all animals share common ancestry?
cliff.prompt: How do we know all animals are related?

options.text: DNA comparison shows shared genetic sequences across all life—the same code, similar genes
options.response: Yes. DNA doesn't lie. All life uses the same genetic language. Shared sequences reveal shared ancestry—even between very different creatures.

options.text: Similar body structures suggest common ancestors that evolved differently
options.response: Anatomy helps, but DNA provides the definitive proof of common ancestry...

q1.title: One Code
q1.script: All life uses the same genetic code—DNA with the same four letters, the same way of encoding proteins. This shared language strongly suggests all life descended from one original organism. Different species, same underlying programming.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "One Code"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: DNA Comparison
q2.script: Compare DNA and you find surprising similarities. Humans and chimps share 98.8% of DNA. Humans and mice share 85%. Even humans and bananas share 60%. The more similar the DNA, the more recent the common ancestor.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Branching Tree
q3.script: Evolution is a branching tree, not a ladder. Species split and split again over millions of years. Every branch connects back eventually to a single trunk—one ancestor from which all animal life diversified.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Diversity arises from unity. All animal variety—millions of species—branched from common origins. We're related to every creature. That connection changes how we might see the natural world.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 135. Tomorrow, we'll explore why we keep pets. Until then, look at an animal and consider: we share ancestors. We're family.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Family Recognition - See the Connection
growTrack.activity: Next time you see an animal—any animal—remember you share ancestors. How many generations back? Millions. But the connection is real. Does knowing this change how you see that bird, that dog, that insect?
